title: Current-canonical replay of atomic accepted water-thermal transaction binding
replays: EB-I10R atomic accepted water-thermal binding without physics or algorithm changes

invariants.assessment: No new kernel is introduced. The existing F-KT and serialized physical runtime remain the sole calculation path.
The new runtime module performs no file, parsing, unit or path I/O and changes no kernel I/O boundary.
Accepted transaction metadata remains separate from parameters, forcing, physical state, numerical configuration and result payloads.
No persistent per-column state is added. Accepted records are ephemeral sparse runtime outputs.
No Newton, Jacobian, constitutive or thermal scratch is moved into column state. Existing worker-local scratch ownership is unchanged.
Binding output is sparse over requested thermal columns and adds only fixed-size scalar metadata per requested record.
The wrapper delegates trial and commit to the existing F-KT/F-MR18 path. Failed thermal trials produce no ready accepted record and do not mutate committed state.
Checkpoint replay, retries and warm-start behavior remain owned by the existing runtime. EB-I10R performs no extra physical run.
The API consumes generic real-valued t0 and t1 and introduces no day, month, year or midnight semantics.
No coupling-window duration is hard coded. The accepted interval is the supplied generic t0,t1 interval.
The workunit supplies transaction provenance infrastructure usable by later coupling/energy composition without weakening existing coupling services.
No groundwater head or flux interface contract is modified.
Existing authoritative water mass accounting is reused unchanged. The wrapper neither alters nor repairs mass residuals.
Interface sensitivity production and ownership are unchanged.
No additional Richards or thermal solve is introduced. Added accepted-column work is fixed-size metadata checking.
The primary API wraps the serialized MultiSWAP runtime, supports sparse column requests and preserves deterministic per-column association.
No MODFLOW cell mapping or one-to-one surface assumption is added.
No deep-vadose component or recharge interpretation is added.
No component-transition storage or flux is modified.
EB-I10R is a current serialized-reference runtime composition and does not alter the common soil-water solver interface. Parallel or alternative backend publication is explicitly not claimed.
Existing Richards, thermal and mass-accounting physics are reused. No legacy global physical state is introduced by EB-I10R.
The new module depends on runtime contracts and does not inspect HeadCalc internal arrays.
Thermal topology admission is checked as physical configuration while numerical policy remains in canonical_numerical_config_t.
No retry ladder or physical iteration is added. Binding cost is bounded metadata validation plus already-existing receipt output.
Reference execution remains unchanged and no production reference mode is removed or bypassed.
Existing column, aggregate and serialized runtime diagnostics pass through unchanged; binding_status adds explicit composition-level failure classification.
Only explicitly requested thermal columns receive receipt/provenance metadata. Nonthermal columns do not gain thermal state or record overhead.
The water-thermal association is implemented in the runtime composition layer, not inside the SWAP kernel or physical process modules.
No assumption about files, .swp input, calendar boundaries, day length or direct MODFLOW attachment is introduced.
This current-canonical replay explicitly records the effect of EB-I10R on all 30 architecture invariants and preserves hard nonclaims.

semantic_attack_review.original_blocker: Two different candidate materializations can share the exposed lineage, origin revision and interval tuple, so post-hoc tuple token authorization cannot prove exact candidate identity.
semantic_attack_review.remediation: Remove the post-hoc candidate/receipt authorization API. The wrapper owns request prevalidation, the single physical runtime call, F-MR18 receipt request and postcommit record materialization in one structural lifecycle.

hard_nonclaims: temperature-field payload contract for energy consumers
vapor snow ice or latent phase-change energy
